Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                Four forces are acting at a point O, of which only three forces and direction of resultant are shown    (5)  
  in figure. If the magnitude of the fourth force is 100N, determine its direction and magnitude of the  
  resultant force.  
  
  
1B)                A ladder of length 7m is placed against a smooth vertical wall. The weight of the ladder is 50N. The (5)  
  lower end of the ladder is 5m from the wall. If the ladder is just to slip, determine the coefficient of  
  friction between the floor and the ladder. Also determine the frictional force acting on the ladder.

3A)   A thin cylindrical shell is 3.5m long and 1m in internal diameter. It is subjected to internal pressure (5)  
  of 1.5 MPa. If the thickness of the sheet is 12mm, determine the circumferential stress, longitudinal  
  stress, changes in diameter and length. Take E=200 GPa and µ= 0.3.  
3B)   Determine the relationship between Young's modulus (E) and Modulus of rigidity (G)                      (5)  
4A)   A bar of steel 50 mm x 50 mm cross section and 150 mm long is subjected to a tensile load of 220        (4)  
  kN along its longitudinal axis and tensile load of 600 kN and 410 kN along lateral axis. Determine  
  the change in each dimension. Given E= 200 GPa µ=0.3

  in an UTM. Indicate the following features on the graph; proportionality limit, elastic limit, yield point,  
  ultimate strength and rupture strength.  
  Distinguish between ultimate strength and rupture strength.
